title: 534,947 New Business Applications. When Does One Break Even?

scenes.vo: Over half a million Americans applied to start a business in September.

captions.text: applied to start a business in September.

scenes.vo: Break-even is the point where sales cover every cost.
Divide monthly fixed costs by what each sale leaves after its own cost.

captions.text: by what each sale leaves after its own cost.

scenes.vo: Illustrative: 3,000 dollars in monthly costs, 3 dollars left per cup. That's 1,000 cups a month.
Census expects about 1 in 18 to become employers within a year. Find your break-even first.

captions.text: to become employers within a year.

applications.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Formation Statistics, September 2026, seasonally adjusted, released 2026-10-14; https://www.census.gov/econ/bfs/current/index.html

projectedFormations.unit: projected business formations with payroll within 4 quarters
projectedFormations.period: September 2026 application cohort, seasonally adjusted (up 1.4% from Aug 2026); a forward projection, not a count
projectedFormations.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Formation Statistics, September 2026, seasonally adjusted, released 2026-10-14; https://www.census.gov/econ/bfs/current/index.html

exampleBreakEven.source: Computed in code: 3,000 / (5 − 2) = 1,000 cups a month; 1,000 / 30 = 33.3, shown as about 34 a day (rounded up)

notes: Many applications are for businesses never meant to hire, so '1 in 18' is not a failure rate.
29,022 is Census's forward projection for the September cohort, not a count of startups.
The coffee cart is illustrative; real break-even also depends on taxes, owner pay and seasonality.
